text:
Kasperi Kapanen has carved out a real role in Edmonton: 18.3 minutes a night, 7 goals and 15 points in 26 games, seven of them on the power play. Yardbarker ran "2 Reasons Kasperi Kapanen Has Found a Home with the Oilers" and Oilersnation asked on Nov. 23, "Is Kapanen the missing piece for the Oilers top line?"

Our numbers are cooler. With him on the ice at 5v5, the Oilers have 46.3% of the attempts and 46.5% of the expected goals (the share of chance quality). His 7 goals come on 4.7 expected, 21% shooting against a talent range near 14.1%, so the scoring has outrun the chances. Last season Evolving-Hockey had his team creating 0.19 fewer expected goals per 60 with him out there, bottom 5% of forwards.

The skills are real. His top speed sits at the very top of NHL Edge tracking, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 80% of his exits leaving the zone with possession last season.

His best night was three points in Florida on Nov. 17. The thing to watch is whether the speed starts producing chances, not just finishes.
